items.title: Verstappen wins a first Singapore Grand Prix, leading throughout from pole
items.summary: Max Verstappen defended against Charles Leclerc into Turn 1, led the whole race and won by 7.335s from Leclerc, with Kimi Antonelli third (+24.573s). Norris, Piastri and Hamilton completed the top six; Lawson, Hulkenberg, Russell and Hadjar took the remaining points. Stroll, Colapinto and Bortoleto retired.
items.why_it_matters: Verstappen's first Marina Bay win at his 10th attempt, from pole, and a repeat of his Sprint victory.

items.title: Hamilton's early stop and second-stop gamble costs Ferrari a podium
items.summary: Hamilton started P3 on mediums and was the first to pit, switching to softs. A later Virtual Safety Car offered a chance at a second stop; he took responsibility for the gamble, calling it a 'painful lesson', and finished sixth. Fred Vasseur called it a mistake that lost a podium. Leclerc held second.
items.why_it_matters: Ferrari left a podium on the table and the Hamilton/Leclerc strategy debrief is the story for the next round.

sources.label: The Race: why Hamilton's race imploded

items.title: Antonelli's podium and Russell's recovery put the title within reach
items.summary: Antonelli finished third while team-mate Russell, starting from the back after a 40-place power-unit penalty, recovered to ninth. Formula1.com reports Antonelli is now 102 points clear and has a first chance to clinch the title. The site's saved standings table may lag the post-race totals.
items.why_it_matters: Formula1.com says the result gives Antonelli his first chance of sealing the title.

items.title: Norris accepts blame for the Sprint clash and finishes fourth, ahead of Piastri
items.summary: Norris now accepts blame for the Sprint collision with Piastri; Andrea Stella called the clash 'serious'. In the race Norris finished fourth and Piastri fifth; Norris said he was not happy with P4 and that McLaren want to fight for wins.
items.why_it_matters: The Sprint collision and the team's response remain a talking point after the race.

sources.label: Formula1.com: Norris not happy with P4

items.title: Racing Bulls will pick their 2027 line-up 'in the coming weeks'
items.summary: Team Principal Alan Permane says Racing Bulls are choosing between three contenders; per Formula1.com every team except Racing Bulls and Haas has said it will keep its current pairing for 2027.
items.why_it_matters: Racing Bulls and Haas are the only teams yet to confirm their 2027 pairings.
